edits.find:
Every abnormal finding is on the left and every one is cerebellar: dysmetria reaching with the left hand, slow rapid alternating movements on the left, and a gait that lists to the left. Cerebellar output decussates twice, so the crossings cancel and cerebellar signs are ipsilateral — which eliminates the right middle cerebellar peduncle in one step.

The pattern also names the part. Limb dysmetria is hemispheric, while a midline vermian lesion gives truncal and gait ataxia with spared limbs. He has both, so the mass is hemispheric and large enough to disturb midline structures — which fits the left facial numbness, since the trigeminal system serves the face ipsilaterally, and the papilledema from fourth-ventricular compression.

edits.find: Headache is a symptom, not a diagnosis. Ask first whether it is primary (migraine, tension-type headache) or secondary, and if secondary, what caused it: a mass (posterior fossa or supratentorial tumor), pressure without a mass (idiopathic intracranial hypertension), blocked CSF flow (hydrocephalus), infection (meningitis, abscess) or bleeding. Primary headaches come and go; secondary headaches progress. Check the vital signs for Cushing triad and fever first. Then the pattern over time, the fundi and the neurologic exam sort the branches; MRI finds the lesion, and tissue, CSF or the typical story confirms it.
edits.with: Ask first whether a headache is primary (migraine, tension-type headache) or secondary. Causes of a secondary headache include a mass (posterior fossa or supratentorial tumor) and pressure without a mass (idiopathic intracranial hypertension). The others are blocked CSF flow (cerebrospinal fluid; hydrocephalus), infection (meningitis, abscess) and bleeding. Primary headaches come and go; secondary headaches progress. Check the vital signs for Cushing triad and fever first. Then use the pattern over time, the fundi and the neurologic exam to sort the causes. MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) finds the lesion. Tissue, CSF or the typical story confirms the diagnosis.
